decisions.reason: As a classic lever-handle line rooted in the firm's established design, engineering and certification knowledge, it is still relatively easy to support and improve, though its maturity and overlap with other handle ranges raise some portfolio-pruning risk.

This handle family remains close to the firm's core architectural-hardware capabilities, so strong absorptive capacity favors incremental refinement and continued commercialization rather than withdrawal.

The single door-handle design fits the firm's existing knowledge base, but as a narrower standalone item it is more exposed than broader families to rationalization within a large and design-led product portfolio.
Because this lever-handle family aligns well with the firm's broad system offer and uses capabilities it already possesses, management would normally keep it and exploit accumulated learning effects.

The electronic access system is closely connected to the firm's strategic move toward digital building organization and builds on its own R&D and system know-how, making continued investment and retention the likely choice.
